newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns Chad over ties with Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China warns Chad over ties with Taiwan.

text.p: China on Wednesday warned Chad of unspecified consequences for recognising its rival Taiwan, but stopped short of announcing the suspension of diplomatic relations with the impoverished African republic.
"The government of Chad... should come back to the correct position or it will face the necessary consequences by the Chinese government," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said by telephone.
The spokesman did not specify what the consequences were, but in the past China has always suspended diplomatic relations with countries that forged ties with Taiwan.

Beijing has considered Taiwan a rebel province without the right to engage in international affairs since the communists won the Chinese civil war and sent the defeated Nationalists fleeing into exile on the island in 1949.
On Tuesday, Taiwan said it had re-established diplomatic relations with Chad, scoring a modest victory in an almost five-decade diplomatic tug-of-war with China.

China has sought to push Taiwan into diplomatic isolation. The rivals have competed aggressively, especially in Africa, for diplomatic recognition, often accusing each other of using large sums of cash and aid to woo potential allies.
"The Taiwan authorities have practised 'money diplomacy'... taking advantage of the economic difficulties of some African countries," the spokesman said.
Chad Foreign Minister Annadif said in Taiwan on Tuesday his country wanted to maintain diplomatic relations with Taipei and Beijing. China said it would not put up with such a formula.
"We will never accept dual recognition," the spokesman said. "We are resolutely opposed to any act of the Taiwan authorities aimed at splitting the motherland.
"The Chinese government will make no compromise at all when it comes to such issues of principle as state sovereignty and national unity," he said.
Taiwan's foreign minister has said the island would offer medical, mechanical and agricultural assistance to Chad, a sprawling former French colony on the fringes of the Sahara desert.

The switch by Chad brought to 31 the number of countries with diplomatic relations with Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government, although that number was expected to fall to 30 at the end of this year when South Africa switches ties to communist China.
